story.headerPrompt: Begin inside the Crimson Spire. Treat transcripts as evidence; merge canon only through validated patches. Secrets stay gm_only until revealed. Pre-296 AC spoiler guard: do not reveal or canonize events after 296 AC unless the player creates them in play.

storyEntries.title: volantis
storyEntries.content: Volantis is the oldest Free City, ruled by three elected Triarchs, and home to Old Blood families inside the Black Walls.

storyEntries.title: old_blood
storyEntries.content: The Old Blood are ancient Volantene noble houses in the Black Walls; only Old Blood members may be elected Triarch.

storyEntries.title: balaerys
storyEntries.content: House Balaerys is the wealthiest Old Blood house; it controls eastern trade, merchant fleets, gold mines, the Crimson Spire, and secretly seeks hereditary Triarch power.

storyEntries.title: vhassar
storyEntries.content: House Vhassar is strong in banking and naval power, owns two war galleys, competes with Balaerys, and secretly excavates a Valyrian steel cache.

storyEntries.title: rhaenysar
storyEntries.content: House Rhaenysar is a martial Old Blood house, bitter rival of Balaerys, with the largest private mercenary force and secret Unsullied plans.

storyEntries.title: nyessos
storyEntries.content: House Nyessos controls grain fleets and farmlands and secretly negotiates a grain pact for blockade leverage.

storyEntries.title: balaerys_heir
storyEntries.content: The player begins as an unnamed scion of House Balaerys with access to the Crimson Spire; exact name, temperament, and succession position are open.

storyEntries.title: folder_scope
storyEntries.content: The folder also contains a 20-house Volantene ledger, 195 custom character/faction lore records, and 57 general ASOIAF world-info records.

storyEntries.title: user_seed_directive
storyEntries.content: User directive: add Westerosi houses, Volantene world rules, general world rules, rank Braavos and Volantis as the strongest Free Cities, mark both as very rich, add economy and war rules, use small details from the World of Ice and Fire lorebook, and avoid spoilers after 296 AC.

storyEntries.title: westerosi_regions
storyEntries.content: Pre-296 source: The North is ruled by House Stark; the Reach by House Tyrell; the Westerlands by House Lannister; the Riverlands by House Tully; the Stormlands by House Baratheon; the Vale by House Arryn; Dorne by House Martell; the Iron Islands by House Greyjoy; the Crownlands by the Iron Throne.

storyEntries.title: braavos
storyEntries.content: Braavos is the wealthiest and most powerful of the Free Cities, ruled by an elected Sealord, guarded by the Titan, home to the Iron Bank and Faceless Men, and slavery is forbidden by its First Law.

storyEntries.title: iron_bank
storyEntries.content: The Iron Bank of Braavos is the wealthiest and most powerful financial institution in the known world; it funds kings and city-states and may support rivals of debtors who fail to repay.

storyEntries.title: economy_rules
storyEntries.content: Pre-296 source synthesis: Westerosi royal finance is handled by the Master of Coin through taxes, crown expenses, and debt management; regional wealth comes from mines, ports, fertile land, fleets, and trade monopolies.

storyEntries.title: war_rules
storyEntries.content: Pre-296 source synthesis: war power depends on sworn houses, regional levies, castles, fleets, commanders, hostages, debt, supply, and geography; the Night Watch remains neutral in realm wars.

storyEntries.title: volantene_rules
storyEntries.content: Volantene canon seed rule: Volantis is ruled by annually elected Triarchs; only Old Blood members are eligible; Old Blood houses inside the Black Walls compete through votes, trade, fleets, private forces, temples, spies, and debts.

storyEntries.title: safe_westerosi_house_bulk
storyEntries.content: Bulk import evidence: safe pre-cutoff House entries from the ASOIAF/Game of Thrones lorebook were promoted into structured house entities/factions. Entries with explicit post-cutoff spoilers were excluded.

storyEntries.title: pre_296_regional_lords
storyEntries.content: Pre-cutoff regional actors used only as faction heads/contacts: Robert Baratheon, Eddard Stark, Tywin Lannister, Jon Arryn, Hoster Tully, Mace Tyrell, Doran Martell, and Balon Greyjoy. No post-cutoff titles or events are imported.

entities.name: House Balaerys
entities.description: Wealthiest Old Blood house; eastern trade, fleets, gold mines, Crimson Spire.

entities.name: House Vhassar
entities.description: Banking and naval Old Blood house; two war galleys; trade competitor.

entities.name: House Rhaenysar
entities.description: Martial Old Blood house with large private mercenary force; Balaerys rival.

entities.name: House Nyessos

entities.description: Continent of the Seven Kingdoms and regional Great House politics.

entities.description: Feudal realm centered on the Iron Throne and regional Great Houses.

entities.name: King's Landing
entities.description: Capital city of the Seven Kingdoms and seat of the Iron Throne.

entities.name: Oldtown
entities.description: Oldest and richest city in Westeros; seat of the Citadel and House Hightower.

entities.name: Braavos
entities.description: Wealthiest and most powerful Free City; home to the Iron Bank and ruled by an elected Sealord.

entities.name: Iron Bank of Braavos
entities.description: Wealthiest and most powerful financial institution in the known world.

entities.name: House Stark
entities.description: Wardens of the North; old First Men line.

entities.name: House Lannister
entities.description: Wealthiest Great House of Westeros through gold and silver mines.

entities.name: House Tyrell
entities.description: Ruling house of the fertile Reach, capable of fielding large armies and tied to the Redwyne fleet.

entities.name: House Baratheon
entities.description: Ruling house of the Stormlands and royal dynasty after Robert’s Rebellion.

entities.name: House Arryn
entities.description: Ruling house of the Vale, protected by mountainous geography and renowned knights.

entities.name: House Tully
entities.description: Ruling house of the fertile but contested Riverlands.

entities.name: House Martell
entities.description: Ruling princely house of Dorne, culturally Rhoynish and historically resistant to conquest.

entities.name: House Greyjoy
entities.description: Ruling house of the Iron Islands, with naval raiding traditions and Iron Fleet power.

entities.name: House Hightower
entities.description: Powerful Oldtown house tied to city wealth, the Hightower, the Citadel, and the Starry Sept.

entities.name: House Dayne
entities.description: House Dayne: An ancient Dornish house of First Men origin, famous for their ancestral sword, Dawn.

state.sigil: A white sword and falling star crossed on a lilac field

entities.name: House Blackwood
entities.description: House Blackwood: An ancient house of First Men origin in the riverlands that remains loyal to the old gods.

state.sigil: A flock of black ravens on scarlet surrounding a dead weirwood

entities.name: House Bracken
entities.description: House Bracken: An old house of First Men descent from the riverlands, perpetual rivals of House Blackwood.

state.sigil: A red stallion on a golden escutcheon on a brown field

entities.name: House Frey
entities.description: House Frey: A relatively young but wealthy and powerful house that controls the crossing of the Green Fork.

state.sigil: Two blue towers on a silver-grey field

entities.name: House Redwyne
entities.description: House Redwyne: A wealthy naval house from the Reach, masters of the Arbor and its world-famous vineyards.

state.sigil: A burgundy grape cluster on a blue field

entities.name: House Cole
entities.description: House Cole: A minor noble house from the Dornish Marches in the stormlands.

state.sigil: Ten black pellets on scarlet, representing lumps of coal

entities.name: House Strong
entities.description: House Strong: An extinct noble house of First Men origin that once held Harrenhal.

state.sigil: A tripartite pale of blue, red, and green on a white field

entities.name: House Reyne
entities.description: House Reyne: An extinct noble house of the Westerlands, formerly the second most powerful house in the region.

state.sigil: A red lion rampant regardant on a silver field

entities.name: House Tarbeck
entities.description: House Tarbeck: An extinct noble house of the Westerlands that shared a common fate with House Reyne.

state.sigil: A seven-pointed star countercharged on gyronny silver and blue

entities.name: House Blackfyre
entities.description: House Blackfyre: An extinct cadet branch of House Targaryen founded by the Great Bastard Daemon Blackfyre.

state.sigil: A black three-headed dragon breathing black fire on a red field

entities.name: House Seaworth
entities.description: House Seaworth: A newly made noble house of the stormlands, founded after Robert's Rebellion.

state.sigil: A black ship with an onion on its sail on a pale grey field

entities.name: House Clegane
entities.description: House Clegane: A house of landed knights in the Westerlands, serving as primary bannermen to the Lannisters.

state.sigil: Three black dogs running on a yellow field

entities.name: House Corbray of Heart's Home
entities.description: House Corbray of Heart's Home: An old but poor noble house from the Vale of Arryn. Their seat is Heart's Home, and they historically claimed the titles of Lord of the Five Fingers and King of the Fingers. Their sigil features three black ravens in flight holding three red hearts on a white field. The house possesses the ancestral Valyrian steel longsword known as Lady Forlorn. Founded during the Andal invasion, they rose to prominence by defeating First Men monarchs.

entities.name: House Waynwood of Ironoaks
entities.description: House Waynwood of Ironoaks: A great noble family of the Vale of Arryn known for their insistence on ceremony and pride. Their seat is Ironoaks, and they blazon their arms with a black broken wheel on a green field. Members of the house typically have brown hair and long faces. They are an old house of high honor, currently fostering the heir presumptive to the Vale, Harrold Hardyng.

entities.name: House Grafton of Gulltown
entities.description: House Grafton of Gulltown: The noble rulers of Gulltown, the only city in the Vale of Arryn. Their sigil is a burning yellow tower within a black pile on a flaming red field. The house was founded by an Andal knight who usurped the city from the First Men House Shett. They control a major port and are noted for staying loyal to the Iron Throne during Robert's Rebellion.

entities.name: House Hunter of Longbow Hall
entities.description: House Hunter of Longbow Hall: A principal noble house of the Vale of Arryn with ancient First Men roots. Their seat is Longbow Hall, located in the eastern Vale. Their sigil depicts five silver arrows fanned on a brown field. Legend states the house joined the realm of the Arryns after an archery contest during the Andal invasion. They are traditionally known for their skill in hunting and archery.

entities.name: House Belmore of Strongsong
entities.description: House Belmore of Strongsong: A powerful house of First Men origin situated at Strongsong in the Vale of Arryn. Their sigil consists of six silver bells arranged 3-2-1 on a purple field. Members of the family are often characterized by red hair. They submitted to House Arryn during the Andal invasion after the defeat of the First Men at the Battle of the Seven Stars.

entities.name: House Templeton of Ninestars
entities.description: House Templeton of Ninestars: A powerful landed knightly house in the Vale of Arryn whose influence is comparable to that of great lords. Their seat is Ninestars, and the head of the house is titled the Knight of Ninestars. Their sigil features nine stars on a gold saltire over a black field. They can easily raise a thousand men and are believed to have blood ties to House Stark.

entities.name: House Cerwyn of Cerwyn
entities.description: House Cerwyn of Cerwyn: One of the closest and most powerful bannermen to House Stark, located only a half day's ride from Winterfell. Their seat is Castle Cerwyn, and their words are 'Honed and Ready'. Their sigil is a black battle-axe on a silver field. Historically, the lords of this house were considered the closest friends of the Starks of Winterfell.

entities.name: House Glover of Deepwood Motte
entities.description: House Glover of Deepwood Motte: A prominent northern house that holds the rank of Master rather than Lord. Their seat is Deepwood Motte in the northwestern wolfswood. Their sigil is a silver mailed fist on a scarlet field. They rule over several petty houses in the wolfswood and were historically First Men kings before being reduced to vassals by the Starks.

entities.name: House Tallhart of Torrhen's Square
entities.description: House Tallhart of Torrhen's Square: A noble northern house of First Men descent that uses the title Master. Their seat is Torrhen's Square, and their words are 'Proud and Free'. Their sigil depicts three green sentinel trees on a brown field. They are among the principal bannermen of Winterfell and are located southwest of the Stark seat.

entities.name: House Hornwood of Hornwood
entities.description: House Hornwood of Hornwood: A principal northern house whose lands border those of House Bolton and House Manderly. Their seat is Hornwood, and their words are 'Righteous in Wrath'. Their sigil is a brown bullmoose with black antlers on an orange field. Their domains include the forest of the Hornwood and reach as far as the White Knife. Their line faced a succession crisis after the deaths of Lord Halys and his heir Daryn.

entities.name: House Ryswell of the Rills
entities.description: House Ryswell of the Rills: A prominent northern family ruling the extensive region known as the Rills. Their sigil is a black horse's head with red eyes and mane on a bronze field with a black border. Individual family members often personalize the horsehead color on their own banners, using grey, brown, or gold. They are an ancient house of First Men origin that once rebelled against the Kings of Winter.

entities.name: House Dustin of Barrowton
entities.description: House Dustin of Barrowton: A major noble house of the north seated at Barrow Hall in the town of Barrowton. Their sigil features two crossed rusted longaxes with a black crown between the points on a yellow field. They claim descent from the First King and the kings of the barrowlands. The house is currently ruled by Lady Barbrey Dustin, who harbors a deep grievance against House Stark.

entities.name: House Flint
entities.description: House Flint: A name shared by several distinct noble houses in the north. Major branches include House Flint of the northern mountains, House Flint of Breakstone Hill, House Flint of Flint's Finger, and House Flint of Widow's Watch. They are of First Men descent and are noted for their varying levels of power and divergent geographic locations.

entities.name: House Crakehall of Crakehall
entities.description: House Crakehall of Crakehall: A primary noble house of the westerlands with First Men roots. Their seat is Crakehall, and their words are 'None so Fierce'. Their sigil is a black and white brindled boar on a brown field. Members are traditionally big-boned and exceptionally strong. They once briefly provided a king to the Iron Islands.

entities.name: House Marbrand of Ashemark
entities.description: House Marbrand of Ashemark: A major noble house of the westerlands formed by the union of First Men and Andal blood. Their seat is Ashemark, and their words are 'Burning Bright'. Their sigil depicts a burning orange tree on a smoke-grey field. They are considered key bannermen of Casterly Rock and are often high in the councils of House Lannister.

entities.name: House Lefford of the Golden Tooth
entities.description: House Lefford of the Golden Tooth: A principal house of the westerlands that controls the Golden Tooth, the main entrance to the west. Their sigil is a golden inverted pile on sky blue with a yellow sun in the canton. The house was established when an Andal warlord married into First Men nobility. They are responsible for the logistics and supplies of the Lannister armies.

entities.name: House Swyft of Cornfield
entities.description: House Swyft of Cornfield: A knightly house from the westerlands seated at Cornfield. Their sigil is a blue bantam rooster on a yellow field, and their words are 'Awake! Awake!'. Though currently knightly, they may have once been a lordly house. The family rose to prominence through the marriage of Dorna Swyft to Kevan Lannister.

entities.name: House Payne
entities.description: House Payne: A noble house of the westerlands and principal bannerman to House Lannister. Their sigil is purple and white chequy with a golden coin in each square. They have produced notable figures such as Ser Ilyn Payne, the King's Justice, and Podrick Payne. The origin of the coins on their arms is associated with an ancient house tale.

entities.name: House Westerling of the Crag
entities.description: House Westerling of the Crag: An ancient but impoverished house of First Men origin from the northwestern westerlands. Their seat is the Crag, and their words are 'Honor, Not Honors'. Their sigil consists of six white seashells on a sand-colored field. Despite their noble lineage, their wealth declined after their gold mines failed.

entities.name: House Brax of Hornvale
entities.description: House Brax of Hornvale: A lordly house from the westerlands and among the chief bannermen to Casterly Rock. Their seat is Hornvale, and their sigil is a purple unicorn on a silver field. The family provides significant heavy cavalry to the Lannister host. They were founded during the Andal invasion of the west.

entities.name: House Oakheart of Old Oak
entities.description: House Oakheart of Old Oak: An ancient and powerful First Men house from the Reach. Their seat is Old Oak, and their words are 'Our Roots Go Deep'. Their sigil depicts three green oak leaves on a gold field. They have a long history of enmity with the Dornish and were founding members of the Kingdom of the Reach.

entities.name: House Rowan of Goldengrove
entities.description: House Rowan of Goldengrove: One of the oldest and most prominent noble families in the Reach. Their seat is Goldengrove, and their sigil is a golden tree on a silver field. They serve as Marshals of the Northmarch and rule over extensive northern territories in the Reach. They trace their descent back to Rowan Gold-Tree, a legendary daughter of Garth Greenhand.

entities.name: House Fossoway
entities.description: House Fossoway: A noble family of the Reach that split into two rival branches. House Fossoway of Cider Hall uses a red apple sigil and is known as the 'red-apple Fossoways'. House Fossoway of New Barrel, founded after a tourney dispute, uses a green apple and is known as the 'green-apple Fossoways'. Both houses trace their origin to the legendary Foss the Archer.

entities.name: House Mullendore of Uplands
entities.description: House Mullendore of Uplands: A lordly house from the Reach that serves as a vassal to House Hightower. Their seat is Uplands, and the family is currently headed by Lord Martyn Mullendore. Members of the house are known for their cheerful dispositions and their history of service in the Reach. They have occasionally married into other high-ranking families like House Templeton.

entities.name: House Yronwood
entities.description: House Yronwood: The most powerful house in Dorne after the ruling Martells. Their seat is Yronwood, a fortress defending the Stone Way into Dorne. The head of the house is known as the Bloodroyal, and the house sigil is a black portcullis grill over sand. They are stony Dornishmen who typically possess blond hair and blue eyes. Historically, the Yronwoods claimed the title High King of Dorne before the arrival of the Rhoynar.

entities.name: House Fowler
entities.description: House Fowler: An ancient First Men family that rules as the Warden of the Prince's Pass. Their seat is Skyreach, and their house words are 'Let Me Soar'. The house sigil depicts a hooded blue hawk on a silver field. In antiquity, the Fowlers reigned as Kings of Stone and Sky and were among the most powerful monarchs in Dorne.

entities.name: House Qorgyle
entities.description: House Qorgyle: A principal noble house of Dorne seated at Sandstone in the western deserts. Their sigil consists of three black scorpions on a red field. Founded by Andal adventurers, the house fortified the only well for fifty leagues to establish their stronghold. They were historically bannermen to House Yronwood before the unification of Dorne under House Martell.

entities.name: House Uller
entities.description: House Uller: A great noble house of Dorne known for a reputation of being impulsive and unpredictable. Their seat is the Hellholt, located deep within the Dornish desert. The house sigil is rayonne yellow over crimson. They are of Andal origin and established their rule during the invasion of Westeros.

entities.name: House Vaith
entities.description: House Vaith: A Dornish house whose head holds the title Lord of the Red Dunes. Their seat is the castle Vaith, located beside the river of the same name. Their sigil is three black leopards standing on a yellow pile on an orange field. The house was established by Andal adventurers during the invasion of Dorne.

entities.name: House Allyrion
entities.description: House Allyrion: A major Dornish noble house seated at Godsgrace near the confluence of the Scourge and the Vaith. Their sigil is a golden hand on gyronny red and black, and their words are 'No Foe May Pass'. Originally founded by Andal adventurers, they were once the overlords of House Martell.

entities.name: House Jordayne
entities.description: House Jordayne: One of the principal noble houses of Dorne, ruling from the Tor on the southern coast of the Sea of Dorne. Their sigil is a golden quill on checkered dark and light green, and their words are 'Let It Be Written'. Founded by Andals, the house was once powerful enough to demand fealty from House Martell.

entities.name: House Santagar
entities.description: House Santagar: A house of landed knights from Spottswood in Dorne. Their sigil is a spotted leopard with a golden axe over a per bend sinister blue and white field. Established by Andal adventurers, they have traditionally been noted for their martial service and sand steeds.

entities.name: House Mallister
entities.description: House Mallister: A prominent noble family from the riverlands whose seat is the coastal fortress Seagard. Their sigil is a silver eagle on indigo, and their house words are 'Above the Rest'. Seagard was built specifically to defend the coastline from ironborn reavers. The house once ruled as independent Kings of the Trident in antiquity.

entities.name: House Piper
entities.description: House Piper: A chief noble house of the riverlands seated at Pinkmaiden Castle. Their sigil depicts a pink dancing maiden in a swirl of white silk over a blue field. Their words are 'Brave and Beautiful'. The house has a history of loyalty to House Tully and famously stood against the Lannisters at the Golden Tooth.

entities.name: House Vance
entities.description: House Vance: A noble house divided into two branches: House Vance of Atranta and House Vance of Wayfarer's Rest. They descend from Armistead Vance, one of the mightiest Andal warlords to invade the riverlands. The house traditionally holds significant influence among the river lords of the Trident.

entities.name: House Roote
entities.description: House Roote: A noble house of the riverlands that rules Lord Harroway's Town. Their historical lineage includes Ser Richard Roote, a founding member of the Kingsguard. The house supported the Blacks during the Dance of the Dragons and remained a prominent vassal in the region.

entities.name: House Mooton
entities.description: House Mooton: A wealthy noble house of the riverlands ruling the port town of Maidenpool. Their sigil is a red salmon on a white field with a gold tressure, and their words are 'Wisdom and Strength'. They claim descent from the First Men and were once independent kings in the Age of Heroes.

entities.name: House Whent
entities.description: House Whent: The last house to legally hold the massive castle Harrenhal before being dispossessed. Their sigil depicts nine black bats on a yellow field. Originally knights in service to House Lothston, they were granted Harrenhal for their role in the Lothstons' downfall. The house is noted for its involvement in the great tourney of 281 AC and its history of subsequent tragedy.

entities.name: House Smallwood
entities.description: House Smallwood: A noble house of the riverlands seated at Acorn Hall. Their sigil is six brown acorns on a yellow field, and their words are 'From These Beginnings'. Though formerly sworn to House Tully, they are currently vassals of House Vance.

entities.name: House Dondarrion
entities.description: House Dondarrion: An old marcher house of the stormlands seated at Blackhaven. Their sigil is a forked purple lightning bolt on a black field speckled with four-pointed stars. The house was founded in the Age of Heroes by a messenger who was saved by lightning during a storm. They are traditional defenders against Dornish incursions.

entities.name: House Selmy
entities.description: House Selmy: A principal marcher house of the stormlands located at Harvest Hall. Their sigil depicts three stalks of yellow wheat on a brown field. Known for producing famed warriors, most notably Ser Barristan the Bold, they are among the most respected families of the Dornish Marches.

entities.name: House Swann
entities.description: House Swann: One of the oldest and most powerful noble houses in the stormlands, ruling from Stonehelm. Their sigil is two battling swans, black and white, on a per pale white and black field. As marcher lords, they control a major river route inland and are regarded as proud and cautious.

entities.name: House Caron
entities.description: House Caron: A principal marcher house ruling from the castle Nightsong. Their sigil is a field of black nightingales on yellow, and their house words are 'No Song so Sweet'. They hold the title Lord of the Marches and claim to be the oldest of the stormlands' marcher lords.

entities.name: House Estermont
entities.description: House Estermont: A noble house of the stormlands ruling from the island of Greenstone. Their sigil is a dark green sea turtle on a pale green field. The house rose to high prominence during the reign of Robert I, who was the son of Lady Cassana Estermont.

entities.name: House Connington
entities.description: House Connington: A noble house of the stormlands seated at Griffin's Roost on Cape Wrath. Their sigil depicts two battling griffins countercharged on a red and white field. Once a wealthy lordly house, they were stripped of much of their land and reduced to landed knights following Robert's Rebellion.

entities.name: House Tarth
entities.description: House Tarth: A noble house that rules the island of Tarth from the seat of Evenfall Hall. Their head is titled the Evenstar, and their sigil is quartered with yellow suns and white crescents on rose and azure. The house has Andal ancestry and historically reigned as independent kings before joining the Storm Kings.

entities.name: House Velaryon
entities.description: House Velaryon: An ancient house of Valyrian descent ruling the island of Driftmark. Their sigil is a silver seahorse on sea green, and their words are 'The Old, the True, the Brave'. Historically the richest house in the Seven Kingdoms under Lord Corlys, they traditionally provide the bulk of the royal fleet.

entities.name: House Celtigar
entities.description: House Celtigar: An ancient and proud house with Valyrian blood, seated on Claw Isle. Their sigil is red crabs strewn on white. They possess a Valyrian steel axe and were among the first houses to support House Targaryen during the Conquest.

entities.name: House Sunglass
entities.description: House Sunglass: A noble house of the crownlands sworn to Dragonstone. Their sigil consists of seven golden seven-pointed stars arranged in a ring on a white field. They are known for their piety and adherence to the Faith of the Seven.

entities.name: House Bar Emmon
entities.description: House Bar Emmon: A noble house from Sharp Point on Massey's Hook in the crownlands. Their sigil is a leaping blue swordfish on fretty silver and white. Founded by Andal warlords, they were once petty kings before yielding to the Storm Kings and later House Targaryen.

entities.name: House Harlaw
entities.description: House Harlaw: One of the most powerful and wealthiest houses of the Iron Islands, ruling the entire island of Harlaw. Their sigil is a silver scythe on black. They rule from the castle of Ten Towers and possess several junior branches across the island.

entities.name: House Goodbrother
entities.description: House Goodbrother: A powerful ironborn house from Great Wyk, seated at the inland castle of Hammerhorn. Their sigil is a gold-banded black warhorn on red. Unlike most major houses of the isles, they claim descent from the Grey King's eldest brother rather than the king himself.

entities.name: House Drumm
entities.description: House Drumm: An ancient ironborn house that rules Old Wyk, the island considered holiest by the ironmen. Their sigil is a white bone hand on a red field. They possess the Valyrian steel sword Red Rain and trace their history back at least eight hundred years.

entities.name: House Botley
entities.description: House Botley: A noble house of the Iron Islands seated at Lordsport on the island of Pyke. Their sigil is a shoal of silver fish on a pale green field. They are one of the primary bannermen to House Greyjoy and control the main port of Pyke.

entities.name: Robert Baratheon
entities.description: King of the Seven Kingdoms and head of the Baratheon royal regime before the cutoff.

entities.name: Eddard Stark
entities.description: Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North.

entities.name: Tywin Lannister
entities.description: Lord of Casterly Rock and principal Lannister power broker.

entities.name: Jon Arryn
entities.description: Lord of the Eyrie and stabilizing elder statesman before the cutoff.

entities.name: Hoster Tully
entities.description: Lord of Riverrun and Riverlands patriarch.

entities.name: Mace Tyrell
entities.description: Lord of Highgarden and Warden of the South.

entities.name: Doran Martell
entities.description: Prince of Dorne and Lord of Sunspear.

entities.name: Balon Greyjoy
entities.description: Lord of the Iron Islands after the failed Greyjoy rebellion.

entityAliases.alias: House Lefford of the Golden Tooth

factions.name: Volantis
factions.description: City-state polity ruled by Triarchs.

factions.name: The Old Blood
factions.description: Volantene houses eligible for Triarch election.

factions.name: House Balaerys
factions.description: Dominant wealthy Old Blood house.

factions.name: House Vhassar
factions.description: Banking and naval Old Blood rival.

factions.name: House Rhaenysar
factions.description: Martial anti-Balaerys rival.

factions.name: House Nyessos
factions.description: Grain and food-supply power.

factions.name: Seven Kingdoms
factions.description: Feudal realm of Westeros ruled through the Iron Throne and Great Houses.

factions.name: Braavos
factions.description: Rank 1 Free City by wealth/power; anti-slavery, Iron Bank, Sealord, Titan.

factions.name: Iron Bank of Braavos
factions.description: Debt and finance power that can fund kings, city-states, or rivals.

factions.name: House Stark
factions.description: Wardens of the North; old First Men line.

factions.name: House Lannister
factions.description: Wealthiest Great House of Westeros through gold and silver mines.

factions.name: House Tyrell
factions.description: Ruling house of the fertile Reach, capable of fielding large armies and tied to the Redwyne fleet.

factions.name: House Baratheon
factions.description: Ruling house of the Stormlands and royal dynasty after Robert’s Rebellion.

factions.name: House Arryn
factions.description: Ruling house of the Vale, protected by mountainous geography and renowned knights.

factions.name: House Tully
factions.description: Ruling house of the fertile but contested Riverlands.

factions.name: House Martell
factions.description: Ruling princely house of Dorne, culturally Rhoynish and historically resistant to conquest.

factions.name: House Greyjoy
factions.description: Ruling house of the Iron Islands, with naval raiding traditions and Iron Fleet power.

factions.name: House Hightower
factions.description: Powerful Oldtown house tied to city wealth, the Hightower, the Citadel, and the Starry Sept.

factions.name: House Dayne
factions.description: House Dayne: An ancient Dornish house of First Men origin, famous for their ancestral sword, Dawn.

factions.name: House Blackwood
factions.description: House Blackwood: An ancient house of First Men origin in the riverlands that remains loyal to the old gods.

factions.name: House Bracken
factions.description: House Bracken: An old house of First Men descent from the riverlands, perpetual rivals of House Blackwood.

factions.name: House Frey
factions.description: House Frey: A relatively young but wealthy and powerful house that controls the crossing of the Green Fork.

factions.name: House Redwyne
factions.description: House Redwyne: A wealthy naval house from the Reach, masters of the Arbor and its world-famous vineyards.

factions.name: House Cole
factions.description: House Cole: A minor noble house from the Dornish Marches in the stormlands.

factions.name: House Strong
factions.description: House Strong: An extinct noble house of First Men origin that once held Harrenhal.

factions.name: House Reyne
factions.description: House Reyne: An extinct noble house of the Westerlands, formerly the second most powerful house in the region.

factions.name: House Tarbeck
factions.description: House Tarbeck: An extinct noble house of the Westerlands that shared a common fate with House Reyne.

factions.name: House Blackfyre
factions.description: House Blackfyre: An extinct cadet branch of House Targaryen founded by the Great Bastard Daemon Blackfyre.

factions.name: House Seaworth
factions.description: House Seaworth: A newly made noble house of the stormlands, founded after Robert's Rebellion.

factions.name: House Clegane
factions.description: House Clegane: A house of landed knights in the Westerlands, serving as primary bannermen to the Lannisters.

factions.name: House Corbray of Heart's Home
factions.description: House Corbray of Heart's Home: An old but poor noble house from the Vale of Arryn. Their seat is Heart's Home, and they historically claimed the titles of Lord of the Five Fingers and King of the Fingers. Their sigil features three black ravens in flight holding three red hearts on a white field. The house possesses the ancestral Valyrian steel longsword known as Lady Forlorn. Founded during the Andal invasion, they rose to prominence by defeating First Men monarchs.

factions.name: House Waynwood of Ironoaks
factions.description: House Waynwood of Ironoaks: A great noble family of the Vale of Arryn known for their insistence on ceremony and pride. Their seat is Ironoaks, and they blazon their arms with a black broken wheel on a green field. Members of the house typically have brown hair and long faces. They are an old house of high honor, currently fostering the heir presumptive to the Vale, Harrold Hardyng.

factions.name: House Grafton of Gulltown
factions.description: House Grafton of Gulltown: The noble rulers of Gulltown, the only city in the Vale of Arryn. Their sigil is a burning yellow tower within a black pile on a flaming red field. The house was founded by an Andal knight who usurped the city from the First Men House Shett. They control a major port and are noted for staying loyal to the Iron Throne during Robert's Rebellion.

factions.name: House Hunter of Longbow Hall
factions.description: House Hunter of Longbow Hall: A principal noble house of the Vale of Arryn with ancient First Men roots. Their seat is Longbow Hall, located in the eastern Vale. Their sigil depicts five silver arrows fanned on a brown field. Legend states the house joined the realm of the Arryns after an archery contest during the Andal invasion. They are traditionally known for their skill in hunting and archery.

factions.name: House Belmore of Strongsong
factions.description: House Belmore of Strongsong: A powerful house of First Men origin situated at Strongsong in the Vale of Arryn. Their sigil consists of six silver bells arranged 3-2-1 on a purple field. Members of the family are often characterized by red hair. They submitted to House Arryn during the Andal invasion after the defeat of the First Men at the Battle of the Seven Stars.

factions.name: House Templeton of Ninestars
factions.description: House Templeton of Ninestars: A powerful landed knightly house in the Vale of Arryn whose influence is comparable to that of great lords. Their seat is Ninestars, and the head of the house is titled the Knight of Ninestars. Their sigil features nine stars on a gold saltire over a black field. They can easily raise a thousand men and are believed to have blood ties to House Stark.

factions.name: House Cerwyn of Cerwyn
factions.description: House Cerwyn of Cerwyn: One of the closest and most powerful bannermen to House Stark, located only a half day's ride from Winterfell. Their seat is Castle Cerwyn, and their words are 'Honed and Ready'. Their sigil is a black battle-axe on a silver field. Historically, the lords of this house were considered the closest friends of the Starks of Winterfell.

factions.name: House Glover of Deepwood Motte
factions.description: House Glover of Deepwood Motte: A prominent northern house that holds the rank of Master rather than Lord. Their seat is Deepwood Motte in the northwestern wolfswood. Their sigil is a silver mailed fist on a scarlet field. They rule over several petty houses in the wolfswood and were historically First Men kings before being reduced to vassals by the Starks.

factions.name: House Tallhart of Torrhen's Square
factions.description: House Tallhart of Torrhen's Square: A noble northern house of First Men descent that uses the title Master. Their seat is Torrhen's Square, and their words are 'Proud and Free'. Their sigil depicts three green sentinel trees on a brown field. They are among the principal bannermen of Winterfell and are located southwest of the Stark seat.

factions.name: House Hornwood of Hornwood
factions.description: House Hornwood of Hornwood: A principal northern house whose lands border those of House Bolton and House Manderly. Their seat is Hornwood, and their words are 'Righteous in Wrath'. Their sigil is a brown bullmoose with black antlers on an orange field. Their domains include the forest of the Hornwood and reach as far as the White Knife. Their line faced a succession crisis after the deaths of Lord Halys and his heir Daryn.

factions.name: House Ryswell of the Rills
factions.description: House Ryswell of the Rills: A prominent northern family ruling the extensive region known as the Rills. Their sigil is a black horse's head with red eyes and mane on a bronze field with a black border. Individual family members often personalize the horsehead color on their own banners, using grey, brown, or gold. They are an ancient house of First Men origin that once rebelled against the Kings of Winter.

factions.name: House Dustin of Barrowton
factions.description: House Dustin of Barrowton: A major noble house of the north seated at Barrow Hall in the town of Barrowton. Their sigil features two crossed rusted longaxes with a black crown between the points on a yellow field. They claim descent from the First King and the kings of the barrowlands. The house is currently ruled by Lady Barbrey Dustin, who harbors a deep grievance against House Stark.

factions.name: House Flint
factions.description: House Flint: A name shared by several distinct noble houses in the north. Major branches include House Flint of the northern mountains, House Flint of Breakstone Hill, House Flint of Flint's Finger, and House Flint of Widow's Watch. They are of First Men descent and are noted for their varying levels of power and divergent geographic locations.

factions.name: House Crakehall of Crakehall
factions.description: House Crakehall of Crakehall: A primary noble house of the westerlands with First Men roots. Their seat is Crakehall, and their words are 'None so Fierce'. Their sigil is a black and white brindled boar on a brown field. Members are traditionally big-boned and exceptionally strong. They once briefly provided a king to the Iron Islands.

factions.name: House Marbrand of Ashemark
factions.description: House Marbrand of Ashemark: A major noble house of the westerlands formed by the union of First Men and Andal blood. Their seat is Ashemark, and their words are 'Burning Bright'. Their sigil depicts a burning orange tree on a smoke-grey field. They are considered key bannermen of Casterly Rock and are often high in the councils of House Lannister.

factions.name: House Lefford of the Golden Tooth
factions.description: House Lefford of the Golden Tooth: A principal house of the westerlands that controls the Golden Tooth, the main entrance to the west. Their sigil is a golden inverted pile on sky blue with a yellow sun in the canton. The house was established when an Andal warlord married into First Men nobility. They are responsible for the logistics and supplies of the Lannister armies.

factions.name: House Swyft of Cornfield
factions.description: House Swyft of Cornfield: A knightly house from the westerlands seated at Cornfield. Their sigil is a blue bantam rooster on a yellow field, and their words are 'Awake! Awake!'. Though currently knightly, they may have once been a lordly house. The family rose to prominence through the marriage of Dorna Swyft to Kevan Lannister.

factions.name: House Payne
factions.description: House Payne: A noble house of the westerlands and principal bannerman to House Lannister. Their sigil is purple and white chequy with a golden coin in each square. They have produced notable figures such as Ser Ilyn Payne, the King's Justice, and Podrick Payne. The origin of the coins on their arms is associated with an ancient house tale.

factions.name: House Westerling of the Crag
factions.description: House Westerling of the Crag: An ancient but impoverished house of First Men origin from the northwestern westerlands. Their seat is the Crag, and their words are 'Honor, Not Honors'. Their sigil consists of six white seashells on a sand-colored field. Despite their noble lineage, their wealth declined after their gold mines failed.

factions.name: House Brax of Hornvale
factions.description: House Brax of Hornvale: A lordly house from the westerlands and among the chief bannermen to Casterly Rock. Their seat is Hornvale, and their sigil is a purple unicorn on a silver field. The family provides significant heavy cavalry to the Lannister host. They were founded during the Andal invasion of the west.

factions.name: House Oakheart of Old Oak
factions.description: House Oakheart of Old Oak: An ancient and powerful First Men house from the Reach. Their seat is Old Oak, and their words are 'Our Roots Go Deep'. Their sigil depicts three green oak leaves on a gold field. They have a long history of enmity with the Dornish and were founding members of the Kingdom of the Reach.

factions.name: House Rowan of Goldengrove
factions.description: House Rowan of Goldengrove: One of the oldest and most prominent noble families in the Reach. Their seat is Goldengrove, and their sigil is a golden tree on a silver field. They serve as Marshals of the Northmarch and rule over extensive northern territories in the Reach. They trace their descent back to Rowan Gold-Tree, a legendary daughter of Garth Greenhand.

factions.name: House Fossoway
factions.description: House Fossoway: A noble family of the Reach that split into two rival branches. House Fossoway of Cider Hall uses a red apple sigil and is known as the 'red-apple Fossoways'. House Fossoway of New Barrel, founded after a tourney dispute, uses a green apple and is known as the 'green-apple Fossoways'. Both houses trace their origin to the legendary Foss the Archer.

factions.name: House Mullendore of Uplands
factions.description: House Mullendore of Uplands: A lordly house from the Reach that serves as a vassal to House Hightower. Their seat is Uplands, and the family is currently headed by Lord Martyn Mullendore. Members of the house are known for their cheerful dispositions and their history of service in the Reach. They have occasionally married into other high-ranking families like House Templeton.

factions.name: House Yronwood
factions.description: House Yronwood: The most powerful house in Dorne after the ruling Martells. Their seat is Yronwood, a fortress defending the Stone Way into Dorne. The head of the house is known as the Bloodroyal, and the house sigil is a black portcullis grill over sand. They are stony Dornishmen who typically possess blond hair and blue eyes. Historically, the Yronwoods claimed the title High King of Dorne before the arrival of the Rhoynar.

factions.name: House Fowler
factions.description: House Fowler: An ancient First Men family that rules as the Warden of the Prince's Pass. Their seat is Skyreach, and their house words are 'Let Me Soar'. The house sigil depicts a hooded blue hawk on a silver field. In antiquity, the Fowlers reigned as Kings of Stone and Sky and were among the most powerful monarchs in Dorne.

factions.name: House Qorgyle
factions.description: House Qorgyle: A principal noble house of Dorne seated at Sandstone in the western deserts. Their sigil consists of three black scorpions on a red field. Founded by Andal adventurers, the house fortified the only well for fifty leagues to establish their stronghold. They were historically bannermen to House Yronwood before the unification of Dorne under House Martell.

factions.name: House Uller
factions.description: House Uller: A great noble house of Dorne known for a reputation of being impulsive and unpredictable. Their seat is the Hellholt, located deep within the Dornish desert. The house sigil is rayonne yellow over crimson. They are of Andal origin and established their rule during the invasion of Westeros.

factions.name: House Vaith
factions.description: House Vaith: A Dornish house whose head holds the title Lord of the Red Dunes. Their seat is the castle Vaith, located beside the river of the same name. Their sigil is three black leopards standing on a yellow pile on an orange field. The house was established by Andal adventurers during the invasion of Dorne.

factions.name: House Allyrion
factions.description: House Allyrion: A major Dornish noble house seated at Godsgrace near the confluence of the Scourge and the Vaith. Their sigil is a golden hand on gyronny red and black, and their words are 'No Foe May Pass'. Originally founded by Andal adventurers, they were once the overlords of House Martell.

factions.name: House Jordayne
factions.description: House Jordayne: One of the principal noble houses of Dorne, ruling from the Tor on the southern coast of the Sea of Dorne. Their sigil is a golden quill on checkered dark and light green, and their words are 'Let It Be Written'. Founded by Andals, the house was once powerful enough to demand fealty from House Martell.

factions.name: House Santagar
factions.description: House Santagar: A house of landed knights from Spottswood in Dorne. Their sigil is a spotted leopard with a golden axe over a per bend sinister blue and white field. Established by Andal adventurers, they have traditionally been noted for their martial service and sand steeds.

factions.name: House Mallister
factions.description: House Mallister: A prominent noble family from the riverlands whose seat is the coastal fortress Seagard. Their sigil is a silver eagle on indigo, and their house words are 'Above the Rest'. Seagard was built specifically to defend the coastline from ironborn reavers. The house once ruled as independent Kings of the Trident in antiquity.

factions.name: House Piper
factions.description: House Piper: A chief noble house of the riverlands seated at Pinkmaiden Castle. Their sigil depicts a pink dancing maiden in a swirl of white silk over a blue field. Their words are 'Brave and Beautiful'. The house has a history of loyalty to House Tully and famously stood against the Lannisters at the Golden Tooth.

factions.name: House Vance
factions.description: House Vance: A noble house divided into two branches: House Vance of Atranta and House Vance of Wayfarer's Rest. They descend from Armistead Vance, one of the mightiest Andal warlords to invade the riverlands. The house traditionally holds significant influence among the river lords of the Trident.

factions.name: House Roote
factions.description: House Roote: A noble house of the riverlands that rules Lord Harroway's Town. Their historical lineage includes Ser Richard Roote, a founding member of the Kingsguard. The house supported the Blacks during the Dance of the Dragons and remained a prominent vassal in the region.

factions.name: House Mooton
factions.description: House Mooton: A wealthy noble house of the riverlands ruling the port town of Maidenpool. Their sigil is a red salmon on a white field with a gold tressure, and their words are 'Wisdom and Strength'. They claim descent from the First Men and were once independent kings in the Age of Heroes.

factions.name: House Whent
factions.description: House Whent: The last house to legally hold the massive castle Harrenhal before being dispossessed. Their sigil depicts nine black bats on a yellow field. Originally knights in service to House Lothston, they were granted Harrenhal for their role in the Lothstons' downfall. The house is noted for its involvement in the great tourney of 281 AC and its history of subsequent tragedy.

factions.name: House Smallwood
factions.description: House Smallwood: A noble house of the riverlands seated at Acorn Hall. Their sigil is six brown acorns on a yellow field, and their words are 'From These Beginnings'. Though formerly sworn to House Tully, they are currently vassals of House Vance.

factions.name: House Dondarrion
factions.description: House Dondarrion: An old marcher house of the stormlands seated at Blackhaven. Their sigil is a forked purple lightning bolt on a black field speckled with four-pointed stars. The house was founded in the Age of Heroes by a messenger who was saved by lightning during a storm. They are traditional defenders against Dornish incursions.

factions.name: House Selmy
factions.description: House Selmy: A principal marcher house of the stormlands located at Harvest Hall. Their sigil depicts three stalks of yellow wheat on a brown field. Known for producing famed warriors, most notably Ser Barristan the Bold, they are among the most respected families of the Dornish Marches.

factions.name: House Swann
factions.description: House Swann: One of the oldest and most powerful noble houses in the stormlands, ruling from Stonehelm. Their sigil is two battling swans, black and white, on a per pale white and black field. As marcher lords, they control a major river route inland and are regarded as proud and cautious.

factions.name: House Caron
factions.description: House Caron: A principal marcher house ruling from the castle Nightsong. Their sigil is a field of black nightingales on yellow, and their house words are 'No Song so Sweet'. They hold the title Lord of the Marches and claim to be the oldest of the stormlands' marcher lords.

factions.name: House Estermont
factions.description: House Estermont: A noble house of the stormlands ruling from the island of Greenstone. Their sigil is a dark green sea turtle on a pale green field. The house rose to high prominence during the reign of Robert I, who was the son of Lady Cassana Estermont.

factions.name: House Connington
factions.description: House Connington: A noble house of the stormlands seated at Griffin's Roost on Cape Wrath. Their sigil depicts two battling griffins countercharged on a red and white field. Once a wealthy lordly house, they were stripped of much of their land and reduced to landed knights following Robert's Rebellion.

factions.name: House Tarth
factions.description: House Tarth: A noble house that rules the island of Tarth from the seat of Evenfall Hall. Their head is titled the Evenstar, and their sigil is quartered with yellow suns and white crescents on rose and azure. The house has Andal ancestry and historically reigned as independent kings before joining the Storm Kings.

factions.name: House Velaryon
factions.description: House Velaryon: An ancient house of Valyrian descent ruling the island of Driftmark. Their sigil is a silver seahorse on sea green, and their words are 'The Old, the True, the Brave'. Historically the richest house in the Seven Kingdoms under Lord Corlys, they traditionally provide the bulk of the royal fleet.

factions.name: House Celtigar
factions.description: House Celtigar: An ancient and proud house with Valyrian blood, seated on Claw Isle. Their sigil is red crabs strewn on white. They possess a Valyrian steel axe and were among the first houses to support House Targaryen during the Conquest.

factions.name: House Sunglass
factions.description: House Sunglass: A noble house of the crownlands sworn to Dragonstone. Their sigil consists of seven golden seven-pointed stars arranged in a ring on a white field. They are known for their piety and adherence to the Faith of the Seven.

factions.name: House Bar Emmon
factions.description: House Bar Emmon: A noble house from Sharp Point on Massey's Hook in the crownlands. Their sigil is a leaping blue swordfish on fretty silver and white. Founded by Andal warlords, they were once petty kings before yielding to the Storm Kings and later House Targaryen.

factions.name: House Harlaw
factions.description: House Harlaw: One of the most powerful and wealthiest houses of the Iron Islands, ruling the entire island of Harlaw. Their sigil is a silver scythe on black. They rule from the castle of Ten Towers and possess several junior branches across the island.

factions.name: House Goodbrother
factions.description: House Goodbrother: A powerful ironborn house from Great Wyk, seated at the inland castle of Hammerhorn. Their sigil is a gold-banded black warhorn on red. Unlike most major houses of the isles, they claim descent from the Grey King's eldest brother rather than the king himself.

factions.name: House Drumm
factions.description: House Drumm: An ancient ironborn house that rules Old Wyk, the island considered holiest by the ironmen. Their sigil is a white bone hand on a red field. They possess the Valyrian steel sword Red Rain and trace their history back at least eight hundred years.

factions.name: House Botley
factions.description: House Botley: A noble house of the Iron Islands seated at Lordsport on the island of Pyke. Their sigil is a shoal of silver fish on a pale green field. They are one of the primary bannermen to House Greyjoy and control the main port of Pyke.

npcBeliefs.belief: Balaerys dominance should be limited through finance, naval leverage, and old Valyrian assets.

terms: Balaerys treats the protagonist as family.

facts.statement: Only Old Blood members may be elected Triarch.
House Balaerys is the wealthiest and most powerful Old Blood house in the Volantene seed.
House Vhassar is excavating a hidden Valyrian steel cache.
Braavos is rank 1 among the Free Cities for this seed: wealthiest, most powerful, and very rich.
Volantis is rank 2 among the Free Cities for this seed: strongest-tier and very rich, with Triarchy rule and Old Blood wealth.
Westerosi Great Houses anchor regional power through seats, vassals, wealth, oaths, and local geography.
Economy simulation should track taxes, debts, mines, ports, fertile land, fleets, trade monopolies, banking pressure, and supply shocks.
War simulation should track levies, fleets, commanders, castles, terrain, supply, morale, hostages, debt, and alliances.
Seed canon must not include events after 296 AC unless later play creates them.
66 safe pre-cutoff Westerosi house entries were imported as structured house entities/factions; 2 entries were skipped for spoiler-risk review.
